The '''1998–99''' season of the [[Belgian First Division A|Jupiler League]] was held between August 21, 1998, and May 16, 1999.  [[K.R.C. Genk|Racing Genk]] became champions.

These teams were promoted from the [[Belgian Second Division|second division]] at the start of the season:
*[[K.V. Oostende|Oostende]] (second division champions)
*[[K.V. Kortrijk|Kortrijk]] (playoff winner)

==Relegated teams==
These teams were relegated to the second division at the end of the season:
*[[K.V. Kortrijk|Kortrijk]]
*[[K.V. Oostende|Oostende]]

==Genk's title success==
After a deceiving start of the competition Anderlecht managed to come back at the top of the ranking under the management of [[Jean Dockx]] and [[Franky Vercauteren]] even beating its long-time rival [[Standard Liège]] in a memorable 0-6 demonstration.  Two matches before the end of the season, the ranking was as such:
{| class="wikitable"
! Pos !! Team !! Pld !! Pts
|-
| 1. ||Genk       ||32 ||70
|-
| 2. ||Brugge     ||32 ||68
|-
| 3. ||Anderlecht ||32 ||64
|}
Those three teams were thus still able to win the championship.  While [[Club Brugge]] lost its game to [[R.E. Mouscron|Mouscron]] 2-0, Anderlecht secured a 2-5 win to Genk.  However the Racing did win its last match at [[K.R.C. Harelbeke|Harelbeke]] and it thus became champion.

==Battle for Europe==
With Genk qualifying for the [[UEFA Champions League]], Anderlecht and Brugge entered the [[UEFA Cup]].

==The relegation dog fight==
[[K.F.C. Lommel S.K.|Lommel]] avoided relegation by winning its last match 2-1 to [[R. Charleroi S.C.|Charleroi]] while the newcomer Kortrijk lost to Anderlecht.  The other newcomer (Oostende) was already relegated at this moment.
